title: Monotonicity, Uniqueness and Frank--Wolfe Dynamics in Atomic Splittable Congestion Games
summary: We study atomic splittable congestion games with $n\ge2$ players and nondecreasing $C^2$ resource costs $f$ with convex $x\mapsto xf(x)$. We characterize the largest resource cost class for which the Nash equilibrium is unique. This characterization combines a curvature inequality involving the first two derivatives and the number of players with strict increase of the scalar marginal costs $x\mapsto f(x)+xf'(x)$.
